name: Sensitivity tornado
reader_question: Which input assumptions move a model output most, and by how much either way?
relationship: One-at-a-time sensitivity: for each driver, the model's lowest and highest outcome around a base case, sorted by swing.
use_when: A model output exists with a stated base case and a low and high outcome for each driver
The reader needs the ranking of drivers by influence, labelled as model output
avoid_when: The figures are observed data rather than model output
Drivers interact strongly — one-at-a-time bars would mislead; show a sensitivity-grid for two drivers
Nothing in the record states the model's assumptions

data_contract.notes: Output measure labelled as model output, and the base-case value
Driver with its tested range, e.g. ±20%
Lowest and highest outcome for that driver; low ≤ base ≤ high

units: One output unit; bars are deviations from the base case, centred on it, with outcome values at the ends.

editable: Stacked bar chart of deviations from base with embedded workbook (Edit Data)
not_data_bound: Chart series hold outcome minus base, not the outcomes themselves
Outcome values at bar ends, the base-case label and the model-output tag are positioned text and shapes computed from the fixture

table_alternative: A table of drivers with tested range, low outcome, high outcome and swing.
variations: Per-scenario base cases in small multiples
limitations: One-at-a-time variation hides interactions between drivers
Bar length depends on the tested ranges chosen, which are assumptions

excluded_alternatives.form: Clustered bars of low and high
excluded_alternatives.reason: Hides the shared base case and makes swing size hard to read
Many overlapping lines on a radial scale obscure the ranking
